item.title: On potential density of rational points on hyperkahler varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.00311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties in each of the four known deformation families admitting a rational Lagrangian fibration are potentially dense. Furthermore, we give several applications and construct examples of hyperk\"ahler varieties beyond these families satisfying the potential density property. Our approach is first to prove that rational points on hyperk\"ahler varieties admitting two rational Lagrangian fibrations with distinct associated isotropic rays are potentially dense. We then construct a projective Shafarevich--Tate twist admitting two such fibrations, together with a dominant rational map from the twist to the original variety.
item.dc:creator: Ting Gong

item.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.00813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Arora, Vivek Mohan Mallick

item.title: Regions of totally real arrangements of rational curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.00861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a plane-curve analogue of Zaslavsky's theorem for arrangements of real rational curves for which every complex singularity with more than one local branch is real and all of its branches are real. If at least one component has odd degree, the number of real regions equals the total rational Betti number of the complexified complement. We also give a formula for bounded affine regions which records the number of branches at infinity and the connected components of the real affine curve. Oriented regions generate the middle Borel--Moore homology over $\mathbb{Q}$, and they generate it over $\mathbb{Z}$ when the component degrees are coprime. The relations are described by the circles in the real normalization and, in an affine chart, by winding functions. These results imply equality of combinatorial rank and real combinatorial rank in the framework of Brown--Dupont and Sturmfels--Telen. Examples include singular rational cubics, arrangements of conics, Chebyshev curves, and the plane model of the $27$ lines on a split cubic surface.
item.dc:creator: Masahiko Yoshinaga

item.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.00864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu

item.title: Galois Actions on Energy-Harmonic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.00990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the action of $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on the solutions to the discrete Dirichlet problem for a graph with fixed edge energies. We establish transitivity of the Galois action outside a thin set in the parameter space and demonstrate that the exceptional thin set may be Zariski dense, so the conclusion cannot in general be replaced by one that holds on a Zariski-open set. Identifying the parameter locus where the Galois action is transitive constrains the possibilities for linking combinatorial and arithmetic properties of the discrete energy-harmonic Laplace equations and other systems of the same form.
item.dc:creator: Bella Finkel

item.title: On motivic multiplicativity of cyclic covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.01008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$ with trivial Chow groups, and let $f: X\rightarrow Y$ be a cyclic cover of degree $d$ branched over a smooth ample divisor $D\in |dL|$. We show that a naturally constructed Chow--K\"unneth decomposition of $X$ is $m$-fold $mn$-multiplicative for each integer $m\geq2$ and that its stable motivic multiplicativity defect satisfies $\mathfrak{sd}(X)\leq 2dn$. If, in addition, each positive-codimension cycle class on $Y$ is supported on $D$, then a double cover admits motivic $0$-multiplicativity. As a further application, we show that any smooth Gushel--Mukai sixfold admits motivic 0-multiplicativity. Moreover, we establish the sharp modified-diagonal property for all smooth double EPW sextics, confirming a conjecture of O'Grady for these varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ze Xu

item.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Bich Van, Nguyen Trung Kien

item.title: Seshadri functions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. At a maximal class $L$, differentiability is equivalent to every curve $C$ computing the Seshadri constant satisfying $\frac{[C]}{{\rm mult}_x C}=\frac{[L]}{\sqrt{L^{2}}}$. We also prove that the non-differentiability locus is nowhere dense. For the blow-up of $\mathbb P^{2}$ at $r\ge 9$ very general points, assuming the $(-1)$-curves conjecture for the blow-up at $r+1$ very general points, we construct a non-empty open subset of the ample cone on which the Seshadri function at a very general point equals $\sqrt{L^{2}}$. Consequently, this function is not piecewise linear. Under the assumption of the Strong SHGH conjecture, we obtain a common non-empty open subset on which maximality holds at every point when $r\ge36$.
item.dc:creator: Cyril J. Jacob

item.title: Hodge theory and topology of Bogomolov--Guan manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bogomolov--Guan manifolds are simply connected, irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds that are not K\"ahler, yet they echo hyperk\"ahler geometry in striking ways. We show that their Fr\"olicher spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ and that their Hodge numbers are stable under small deformations. The general fibers of their natural Lagrangian fibration are rationally null-homologous, and the Beauville--Bogomolov--Fujiki form is degenerate. Despite this, in every dimension, the Euler characteristics agree with those of generalized Kummer manifolds. In dimensions four and six, we compute the full Hodge diamonds and all Chern and Pontryagin numbers. Surprisingly, these characteristic numbers are the same as the generalized Kummer ones, even though the Betti numbers differ and the Hodge diamonds are asymmetric.
item.dc:creator: Nikon Kurnosov, \'Angel David R\'ios Ortiz

item.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
item.description: arXiv:2611.01260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.
item.dc:creator: Alex D\"anzer, Yannik Schuler

item.title: Artinian reduction applied to the Largest Intersection Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose we have $r$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^m$ of degree $d$, whose defining polynomials are linearly independent and whose intersection is zero-dimensional. What is the maximum number of points in their intersection? This problem is motivated by computing the generalized Hamming weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, and a conjectured formula for this maximum was given in [21]. We prove the conjectured formula for arbitrary $m$ when $\binom{m+d}{d}-\binom{d+2}{2}<r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. We use the notion of Artinian reduction to reformulate the problem in terms of graded Artinian algebras and then apply combinatorial tools to bound their Hilbert functions.
item.dc:creator: Yuxin Lin

item.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine, Jack J Garzella

item.title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.01423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.
item.dc:creator: Baohua Fu

item.title: Du Bois cohomology of noncommutative spaces and the Hodge numbers invariance conjecture for singular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.01508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the definition of cdh-sheafified Hochschild homology from varieties to stable categories linear over a field of characteristic zero, thereby proving its Morita-invariance. The dimensions of its homology groups give meaningful numerical invariants of a category; we combine them with invariants coming from topological K-theory and Poincar\'e duality to prove equality of mixed Hodge numbers for singular complex projective Fourier--Mukai partners in several classes in dimensions two, three, and four, including normal surfaces and threefolds with rational singularities and equal irregularity. Beyond these applications, we construct Du Bois versions of topological cyclic homology of stable categories together with appropriate multiplicative structures, prove a Geller--Weibel-type result for the variants of negative cyclic homology we introduce, and give categorical characterizations of cohomological purity of proper varieties and the $\mathbb{Q}$-factoriality defect of complex projective threefolds with rational singularities.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Konovalov

item.title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.01528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Shu

item.title: Derived Torelli for Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every orientation-preserving Hodge isometry between the integral Mukai lattices of the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds is induced by an exact equivalence. The proof uses Markman--Mehrotra's comonad reconstruction method to recover both Kuznetsov components from a common Fourier--Mukai comonad on a moduli space of stable objects. As an application, we prove that the Kuznetsov components of two smooth cubic fourfolds are equivalent whenever their Fano varieties of lines are derived equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Hanfei Guo, Ruxuan Zhang

item.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.01745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Markarian

item.title: Moduli spaces of rank 2 sheaves on $\mathbb P^3$ via Quot schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Gieseker--Maruyama moduli space $M_{c_3}$ of stable rank 2 torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^3$ with Chern classes $c_1=-1$, $c_2=1$, and odd $c_3 \le 1$. Every such sheaf $E$ has reflexive hull $E^{\ast\ast}$ parametrised by $M_1$, and the quotient $E^{\ast\ast}/E$ is a 0-dimensional sheaf of length $n = (1-c_3)/2$. We prove that $M_{c_3}$ is isomorphic to the relative Quot scheme $\mathsf{Quot}_{\mathbb{P}^3 \times M_1/M_1}(\mathscr{R},n)$, where $\mathscr{R}$ is the universal reflexive sheaf over $M_1$. Our technique combines (i) Bridgeland-type wall-crossing in Donaldson--Thomas theory, (ii) the theory of good moduli spaces, (iii) deformation theory in dgla and Ext-quiver language. We deduce that $M_{c_3}$ is connected, and we analyse its \emph{smoothable component} $M_{c_3}^{\mathsf{main}}$, proving it is rational and generically smooth of dimension $4n+3$. We further prove that $\dim \mathrm{Sing} M_{c_3} \geq 4n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$. Finally, we provide a geometric characterisation for the cases $n\leq 2$. We show that $M_{-1}$ is a smooth rational projective variety of dimension 7 and compute its motive in the Grothendieck ring of varieties, while $M_{-3}$ is shown to be an integral, normal variety of dimension 11 that is regular in codimension 4.
item.dc:creator: Charles Almeida, Nicol\`o Bignami, Marcos Jardim, Andrea T. Ricolfi

item.title: A Reider-type theorem for syzygies of cyclic covers of anticanonical rational surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\pi\colon X\to S$ be a smooth ramified cyclic cover of an anticanonical rational surface, with $\kappa(X)\geq0$, and let $A$ be a divisor on $S$. We prove a Reider-type theorem for syzygies: for every integer $p\ge 0$, the adjoint divisor $K_X+\pi^*A$ satisfies Property $\mathrm{N}_p$ provided that $A\cdot C\geq p+3$ for every curve $C\subseteq S$ with $C^2\le 1$. One ingredient is a syzygy criterion for finite covers that reduces the weight-two Koszul vanishing on $X$ to weight-one vanishing for the nontrivial character modules on $S$. The most delicate case, in which $\dim|-K_S|=0$ and $K_S^2<0$, is handled by a separate geometric argument.
item.dc:creator: Lei Song

item.title: The Coxeter-Todd abelian sixfold, Gamma00, and big Schottky
item.description: arXiv:2611.02013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We recall the construction of the Coxeter-Todd principally polarized abelian sixfold, and study its special properties. We show that the base locus of the Gamma00 linear system on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold consists of 253 points, disproving the stronger version by Donagi and Beauville--Debarre of the Gamma00 conjecture of van Geemen and van der Geer. This also leads us to construct explicit indecomposable 7-dimensional principally polarized abelian varieties that are not Jacobians, but lie in the so-called Big Schottky locus, thus disproving the corresponding conjecture from the Schottky-Jung approach to the Schottky problem. We furthermore show that while no even theta constant vanishes for the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, its associated Scorza quartic is identically zero. Finally, we show that there exist two different theta level (2,4) structures on the Coxeter-Todd sixfold, for which the sets of second order theta constants are projectively equal. This disproves the expected injectivity of the second order theta constant map for all genera starting with 6.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Grushevsky

item.title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.
item.dc:creator: Ekaterina Bogdanova, Dyne Lee

item.title: Motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces at the characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.02320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a novel, homotopy theoretic model for the motivic Eilenberg--Mac Lane spaces $K(Z_{(p)}(n), 2n) \in Spc(k)$ over fields of characteristic p. Using this, we determine their motives and, consequently, determine the motivic Steenrod algebra at the characteristic. Applications include the Hopkins--Morel isomorphism over arbitrary base schemes as well as the computation of the p-completed motivic stable stems and algebraic cobordism groups of fields of characteristic p. Along the way we expand the theory of normed algebraic structures in motivic homotopy theory, compare them to derived algebra at the characteristic, and produce a functor computing the motivic homology of the $P^1$-loop spaces of (certain) motivic spaces in terms of the motives.
item.dc:creator: Tom Bachmann, Michael J. Hopkins

item.title: Construction of stability conditions on some Kuznetsov components
item.description: arXiv:2611.02388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Bridgeland stability conditions on the Kuznetsov components of smooth Fano hypersurfaces of degrees three, four, and six and dimension at least three, smooth quartic double fivefolds, and smooth Fano complete intersections of three quadrics. For odd-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces and quartic double fivefolds, every connected component of the numerical stability manifold is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C\times\mathbb H$. For general cubic sevenfolds and quartic double fivefolds, spherical twists produce infinitely many distinct connected components.
item.dc:creator: Dongjian Wu

item.title: The topology of the amoeba map and maximal volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.02496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a smooth complete intersection $V\subset(\C^*)^n$ of dimension $k$, $n\ge2k$, we bound the volume of its amoeba by $\pi^{2k}$ times a sum of mixed volumes, divided by the order of any finite group $\Gamma$ of symmetries commuting with the logarithmic map. For $n=2k\ge4$ almost every fibre of the amoeba map has a number of points divisible by $2|\Gamma|$. For $n=2k$ we characterise the varieties of maximal volume, show that for $k\ge2$ they are not real, and prove that no plane in general position in $(\C^*)^4$ has maximal volume. For $n>2k$ the bound is never attained, varieties of maximal volume have amoeba maps injective off a null set, and injectivity is generic. The amoeba map of almost every real $k$-plane is two-to-one, and that of the $k$-th symmetric power of a real line exactly $2^k$-to-one; conversely, real $k$-planes in general position in $(\C^*)^{2k}$ with $2^k$-to-one amoeba maps are symmetric powers. We also classify the real planes of $(\C^*)^4$ and study lines in $(\C^*)^3$.
item.dc:creator: Mounir Nisse

item.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Karpov, Felix Thimm

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential positivity and on solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: Human Variations on AI Mathematics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article is motivated by the OpenAI manuscripts "Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints" and "Log abundance in characteristic zero". We establish a jet comparison for metrics with minimal singularities and use it to prove a dlt-type extension theorem. Combined with geometric arguments from the latter manuscript, this yields an alternative analytic proof of its Theorem~3.1.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Cao, Mihai Paun

item.title: The Universal Nilpotent Cone and a Canonical 1-form
item.description: arXiv:2611.03311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a canonical Du Bois 1-form on the nilpotent cone in the dual Lie algebra of any reductive group. Using this 1-form we give an intrinsic construction of Nadler and Yun's universal global nilpotent cone. In particular, we obtain a moduli interpretation of the universal nilpotent cone.
item.dc:creator: Marius Kj{\ae}rsgaard

item.title: Spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.03464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a formula for the spectral pairs of Newton non-degenerate polynomials with isolated singularities. This is a revised version of a conjecture proposed by Steenbrink fifty years ago. Although this conjecture fails in the non-simplicial Newton polytope case, we can find the correction term using the intersection complexes and the primitive intersection cohomologies of toric varieties associated with non-simplicial compact faces. To verify the correctness of the formula, we provide a sample code for Singular which computes the spectral pairs and compares the output with that of sppairs in Singular for the three variable case.
item.dc:creator: Seung-Jo Jung, In-Kyun Kim, Morihiko Saito, Youngho Yoon

item.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.03514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient is bounded linearly by its volume, with a constant depending only on the complex dimension. This gives a quantitative strengthening of the finiteness theorems of Bader--Fisher--Miller--Stover (Invent. Math., 2023) and Baldi--Ullmo (Ann. of Math., 2023).
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Runze Zhang

item.title: GW/PT-correspondence for CY $4$-fold-II: Virtual Classes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B$ be a complex manifold and $f:\bX\to B$ a derived \textit{complex-analytic} (not necessarily \textit{algebraic}) space with an oriented relative $(-2)$-shifted symplectic structure. We suppose that the closed symplectic form is locally exact in the completed relative de Rham complex, and construct a derived smooth manifold over $B$, independent of additional choices. When $f$ is proper and oriented, this gives integral virtual fundamental classes on its fibres. Our argument is heavily based on the strategy of Borisov-Joyce who already solved the \textit{algebraic} version of this problem, and uses \textit{derived differential geometry}. The proof also contains a relative analytic Darboux theorem a-la Brav-Bussi-Joyce, and has a natural analogue in Borel-Moore homology. We provide applications to complex-analytic enumerative geometry: in particular, to counting Pandharipande-Thomas pairs on compact and non-compact complex-analytic Calabi-Yau $4$-folds. This is part of a joint project with Felix Thimm dedicated to the proof of the GW/PT-correspondence for Calabi-Yau $4$-folds by implementing Pardon's programme in dimension $4$.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Karpov

item.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
item.description: arXiv:2611.03572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.
item.dc:creator: L. Bernal-Gonz\'alez, M. C. Calder\'on-Moreno, J. A. Prado-Bassas

item.title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.00220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Bertoloni Meli, Teruhisa Koshikawa

item.title: Porteous Meets Walsh: Counting Critical Points for $\mathcal{H}_2$-Norm Model Order Reduction Using Algebraic Geometry Behind Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several polynomial systems arising in systems and control have been shown to exhibit a partially linear structure, which allows them to be reformulated as a multiparameter eigenvalue problem (MEP). In this work, we show how such MEP formulations can be leveraged to obtain refined information about the solution set of the polynomial system. We demonstrate, in the setting of single-input single-output $\mathcal{H}_2$-norm model order reduction, how the Thom--Porteous formula can be used to derive an exact count of the complex solutions of the critical equations derived from Walsh's theorem. We prove, under suitable genericity assumptions, that their set of complex solutions is finite and that all solutions occur without multiplicity. Moreover, we derive an explicit formula for the total number of complex solutions as a function of the model orders. Throughout, we provide a self-contained and application-oriented exposition of the algebro-geometric tools required for our analysis, with the aim of making them accessible to the broader engineering community.
item.dc:creator: Sibren Lagauw, Leonie Kayser, Bart De Moor

item.title: Quasi-polynomial valuations of lattice polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for any valuation $\varphi$ of lattice polytopes in ${\mathbb R}^m$, which is quasi-polynomial with respect to ${\mathbb Z}^m$-translations, and any lattice polytope $P$, the function $\varphi(nP)$ is quasi-polynomial in $n$.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr V. Pukhlikov

item.title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
item.description: arXiv:2611.00315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families. We also study the varieties of Jordan algebra structures up to dimension three over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Besides explicit degenerations and standard arguments, we introduce the alicyclic and characteristic conditions as geometric obstructions to degeneration. We determine the rigid algebras and irreducible components in both dimensions. In dimension three, one component is the nine-dimensional affine space of square-zero products; unlike the other three components, it contains no open orbit.
item.dc:creator: Isabel Hernandez, Maria Eugenia Martin, Rodrigo Lucas Rodrigues, Carlos Andre Gomes Silva

item.title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.
item.dc:creator: Jaewon Min

item.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
item.description: arXiv:2611.00457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Canonical quantum curve I
item.description: arXiv:2611.00997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate a canonical quantum curve conjecture $\widehat H\Psi_*=0$ for spectral curves of positive genus. Here $\Psi_*$ is the non-perturbative wave function associated with Eynard--Orantin topological recursion, specialized at the \emph{canonical vanishing point}, a distinguished zero of the closed non-perturbative partition function. The operator $\widehat H$ is obtained by Weyl quantization of $H(x,y)$, with $\widehat x=x\cdot$ and $\widehat y=\hbar\partial_x$, together with quantum corrections to its coefficients. These corrections depend only on closed moduli and $\hbar$ and vanish classically. Whenever a geometric definition is available, we conjecture that the corrected coefficients are suitably normalized Wilson-loop expectation values. When a corresponding refined theory exists, we conjecture a relation between the canonical vanishing point and the closed Nekrasov--Shatashvili free energy. We prove the quantum curve conjecture for Weierstrass curves and the mirror curves of canonical bundles of smooth projective toric weak del Pezzo surfaces, including local $\mathbb P^2$. For the local surfaces considered here, we relate the canonical vanishing point to a derivative of the closed NS free energy. For local $\mathbb P^2$, we also identify the corrected coefficient with a suitably normalized, geometrically defined NS Wilson-loop expectation value.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

item.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursions for Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes on Moduli Spaces of Super Riemann Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive an Eynard-Orantin topological recursion for intersection numbers involving Norbury's $\Theta$-class together with $\psi$-classes and higher $\kappa$-classes. These intersection numbers encode higher Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super Riemann surfaces. The resulting recursion is a higher-$\kappa$ deformation of the topological recursion associated with the Bessel curve, which encodes the Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten model.
item.dc:creator: Dingkang Xiong, Jian Zhou

item.title: MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.01546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<\rho<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloor\rho n\rfloor,n-\lfloor\rho n\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Guorui Ma

item.title: Absolute descent and the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.01654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the programme developed in Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory by studying descent for augmented pseudocosimplicial objects. Let $\mathcal H$ be a $2$-category, and let $\operatorname{suc}=\mathsf{1}+(-)$ be the successor monad on the augmented simplex category. Precomposition with $\operatorname{suc}$ induces the d\'ecalage pseudomonad $\mathbb S$ on the $2$-category of augmented pseudocosimplicial objects with values in $\mathcal H$. We prove that every successor contraction makes the corresponding augmented pseudocosimplicial object effective for descent. This structure is preserved by postcomposition with every pseudofunctor. Consequently, the resulting descent object is an absolute bilimit. A first application concerns split epimorphisms. We recover the Janelidze--Tholen characterization of absolute effective descent morphisms given in Facets of Descent II. Moreover, we prove that one direction holds for every pseudofunctor $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, where $\mathcal H$ is an arbitrary $2$-category. Consequently, every $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra is of absolute descent. In particular, this holds for every free $\mathbb S$-pseudoalgebra, and hence for every one-sided d\'ecalage. This makes the shift-effectiveness hypothesis in the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem of Pseudo-Kan extensions and descent theory automatic. Thus, under the adjointness and Beck--Chevalley hypotheses, the descent and Eilenberg--Moore factorizations are equivalent whenever they exist. We thus obtain a stronger version of the B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem for arbitrary augmented pseudocosimplicial objects, which we call the formal B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem. Applied to indexed \v{C}ech objects associated with pseudofunctors $A\colon C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal H$, this theorem extends the classical B\'enabou--Roubaud theorem to an arbitrary $2$-category $\mathcal H$.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Lucatelli Nunes

item.title: A Global Generic Locus for Elementary Abelian p-covers of P^1 with two Ramification Points
item.description: arXiv:2611.02398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study elementary abelian $p$-covers of $P^1$ totally ramified at exactly two points and unramified elsewhere. Such covers are isomorphic to the rank-$\ell$ Artin--Schreier curves $ X_{f, \ell} : y^{p^\ell} - y = f(x), $ where $f \in \bar{F}_p[x^{\pm 1}]$ has a pole of order $d_1>0$ at $0$ and order $d_2>0$ at $\infty$. After fixing $d_1$ and $d_2$, the cover $X_{f, \ell}$ is generic if its Newton polygon is minimal as $f$ varies over all Laurent polynomials with pole orders $d_1$ and $d_2$. For $p$ sufficiently large relative to $d_1$ and $d_2$, we construct a combinatorial cost polygon $GL(d_1,d_2,p)$ and prove that its attainment is characterized by the nonvanishing of a homogeneous polynomial in the coefficients of $f$. Moreover, we prove that these conditions stabilize: there exists a Zariski-open dense subset $U$ in the coefficient space that is defined over $\Q$ and depends only on $d_1$ and $d_2$, whereby for any $f$ whose coefficients lie in $U(\overline{\Q})$, the reduction is generic at every prime ideal above sufficiently large rational primes, and for every rank $\ell$ permitted by the residue field. This result extends Zhu's result for one ramification point.
item.dc:creator: Robert Moore, Hui June Zhu

item.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
item.description: arXiv:2611.02417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.
item.dc:creator: Peter Koroteev

item.title: $S_n$-equivariant $L$-classes of Cartesian powers of Witt spaces and the Hodge index conjecture for symmetric products
item.description: arXiv:2611.02577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a compact oriented even-dimensional Witt pseudomanifold $X$, we compute the $S_n$-equivariant Banagl--Zagier $L$-classes of $X^n$ in terms of the Goresky--MacPherson $L$-classes of $X$ and the intersection cohomology Euler characteristic of $X$. This generalizes a theorem of Zagier for manifolds. Our approach is based on analyzing the equivariant structure of the signature operator of $X^n$ using equivariant $KK$-theory and power operations in analytic $K$-homology. We establish an analytic $K$-homology analogue of Moonen's algebraic localization theorem by proving that the localized Chern character of the $n$-th power operation, evaluated at an $n$-cycle, agrees with the $n$-th homological Adams operation applied to the Chern character. As an application, we prove that the characteristic class Hodge index conjecture for singular varieties, formulated by Brasselet--Sch\"urmann--Yokura, is preserved under taking symmetric products of complex projective varieties.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadali Aligholi

item.title: Characterization of the boundary zero set of stable polynomials in $\mathbb B_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a polynomial $p\in \mathbb{C}[z,w]$ whose zeros lie outside the unit ball $\mathbb{B}_2$ of $\mathbb{C}^2,$ we study its local Weierstrass polynomial--obtained via the Weierstrass Preparation Theorem--and provide a strong version of the Nash curve selection lemma. These results lead to a characterization of the intersection of the zero set of $p$ with the unit sphere: $\mathcal{Z}(p)\cap\mathbb{S}_{2}.$
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Vavitsas

item.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.02967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space. In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds. Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fej\'er--Riesz theorem yields certificates.
item.dc:creator: Abhay Jindal, Alja\v{z} Zalar

item.title: Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.03036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.
item.dc:creator: Antoine de Saint Germain, Robin Zhang

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the singular loci of the reduced $\SL_2(\CC)$-representation varieties $R_{m,n}$ of non-Hopfian Baumslag--Solitar groups $B(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid b^{-1}a^m b=a^n\rangle$. We determine their dimensions and profile functions, which list the numbers of irreducible components in descending order of dimension. The components have dimensions three or five. Their reduced singular loci have the explicit description \[ \Sing R_{m,n} =\left\{(\varepsilon I,Y): \varepsilon^m=\varepsilon^n,\quad (\tr Y)^2=\frac{(m+n)^2}{mn}\right\}, \] where $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ and $Y\in\SL_2(\CC)$. Each is a disjoint union of $\mu$ copies of the smooth affine quadric $Q=\{(x,y,z)\in\CC^3:x^2+yz=1\}$, where $\mu=2$ for $m-n$ odd and $\mu=4$ for $m-n$ even. Thus its complex algebraic isomorphism type depends only on this parity. Each quadric is homotopy equivalent to $S^2$, so the singular locus has integral homology $\ZZ^\mu$ in degrees zero and two and zero in all other degrees. An algebraic stratification gives its compactly supported E-polynomial $\mu(q^2+q)$, with $q=uv$. At every singular point, $R_{m,n}$ is locally analytically the product of a smooth surface and a nodal curve.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Isogeny rigidity under algebraic group actions and finite translation orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.03606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite orbits generated by fibrewise translations on varieties carrying two abelian fibrations. Under natural dominance and generation hypotheses, non-isotriviality of the first family forces points with finite orbit to lie over proper closed subsets of both bases. This extends results of Corvaja, Tsimerman and Zannier to complex families of arbitrary, possibly different relative dimensions, including torsors. The proof combines relative Manin-Mumford with a general isogeny rigidity theorem for algebraic group actions.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Dolce, Francesco Tropeano, Ekaterina Amerik

item.title: Intersection theory on derived stacks
item.description: arXiv:1909.01332v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define integral cycle complexes and Chow homology of derived Artin stacks. To any quasi-smooth family of derived Artin stacks we associate a bivariant fundamental class, encoding the virtual fundamental classes of its fibres and their deformation invariance up to coherent homotopy. We extend the Riemann-Roch theorem of Baum-Fulton-MacPherson from quasi-projective schemes to derived Artin stacks, and thereby obtain a virtual Riemann-Roch formula for quasi-smooth derived Artin stacks. As another application of the formalism, we construct intersection products on regular Artin stacks locally of finite type over a field. Finally, we prove an integral comparison of our Chow homology with the cycle-theoretic Chow groups of Kresch.
item.dc:creator: Adeel A. Khan

item.title: Complements of discriminants of real singularities of type $X_{10}$
item.description: arXiv:2301.06994v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Conjecturally complete lists of connected components of the complements of the discriminant varieties (aka wave fronts) of smooth function singularities of types $X_{10}^3$ and $X_{10}^1$ are provided. The combinatorial invariants of these components are defined and calculated. It is shown that the one-dimensional homology group of the complement of the discriminant of any versal deformation of any singularity of class $X_{10}^1$ contains a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^3$.
item.dc:creator: Victor A. Vassiliev

item.title: The Complete Intersection Discrepancy of a Curve II: Families of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2310.16558v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study equisingularity of families of reduced curves over smooth parameter spaces of arbitrary positive dimension, using the difference between two analytic invariants of a curve singularity: the multiplicity of its Jacobian ideal and its complete intersection discrepancy. This difference provides a fiberwise multiplicity criterion for Whitney equisingularity. We prove that Whitney equisingularity (equivalently, strong simultaneous resolution) is characterized by equidimensionality of the fibers of the exceptional locus of either the relative conormal space or the relative Nash blowup. We further show that this condition is equivalent to the emptiness of the relative polar variety of smallest dimension. In addition, we establish that the Milnor number of a reduced curve is Zariski upper semicontinuous. As an application, we show that the constancy of the Milnor number in a family of reduced curves is equivalent to its topological equisingularity, under a natural assumption on the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Bengu\c{s}-Lasnier, Terence Gaffney, Antoni Rangachev

item.title: Quasi-$F^e$-splittings and quasi-$F$-regularity
item.description: arXiv:2404.06788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the theory of quasi-$F^e$-splittings, quasi-$F$-regularity, and quasi-$+$-regularity.
item.dc:creator: Hiromu Tanaka, Jakub Witaszek, Fuetaro Yobuko

item.title: Algebraically trivial automorphisms of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2407.06007v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS) manifold $X$, we call an automorphism $f$ of $X$ algebraically trivial if $f$ acts trivially on the N\'eron--Severi group of $X$. In this paper, we extend the approach of Brandhorst--Cattaneo to classify, by means of lattice data, all the pairs $(X, G)$, where $X$ is an IHS manifold of a known deformation type (to this date), and $G$ is a finite group consisting of algebraically trivial automorphisms of $X$ that are nonsymplectic. In particular, we classify even-order algebraically trivial nonsymplectic automorphisms, with or without trivial discriminant action. In the case of nontrivial discriminant actions, we show that such automorphisms only exist for finitely many deformation types and orders
item.arxiv:journal_reference: \'Epijournal de G\'eom\'etrie Alg\'ebrique, volume 10 (2026), article no. 20
item.dc:creator: Stevell Muller

item.title: Some applications of the Nygaard filtration and quasisyntomic descent in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2507.08568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article gives an expository account of quasisyntomic descent and the Nygaard filtration in positive characteristic, complemented by several new applications to $p$-adic cohomology theories. The guiding result is a new approach to Illusie's comparison between fppf cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_p(1)$ coefficients and the slope $1$ part of crystalline cohomology. We follow work of Bhatt-Lurie, but give a more elementary presentation which does not rely on the formalism of $\infty$-categories. We then revisit Ogus' comparison theorem between infinitesimal cohomology and \'etale cohomology, and give new proofs of several results on fppf cohomology that were previously obtained with the de Rham-Witt complex. We also determine the action of multiplication-by-$n$ on the fppf cohomology of an abelian variety, answering a question of A. Skorobogatov to the author. This is an expanded version of the author's master thesis.
item.dc:creator: Livia Grammatica

item.title: A Microlocal Theory for Zariski-Constructible Sheaves on Rigid Analytic Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2507.18604v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a microlocal theory, in the sense of Kashiwara-Schapira, for Zariski-constructible sheaves on rigid analytic varieties. We define and study monodromic sheaves, the monodromic Fourier transform, specialisation, microlocalisation, micro-hom, and singular support in this context. Some questions and conjectures are formulated in the end. The appendix contains infinity-categorical characterisations of monodromic sheaves.
item.dc:creator: Tong Zhou

item.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds via Brill-Noether theory of curves
item.description: arXiv:2509.24990v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fix a polarised Calabi-Yau threefold $(X,H)$. We reduce a version of the Bayer-Macr\`i-Toda conjecture for $(X,H)$, which ensures the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$, to verifying a Brill-Noether-type inequality for curves on $X$. We then prove this inequality for a broad class of Calabi-Yau threefolds, including complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefolds in weighted projective spaces.
item.dc:creator: Soheyla Feyzbakhsh, Naoki Koseki, Zhiyu Liu, Nick Rekuski

item.title: Base Change Of Fundamental Group Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2602.11110v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K/k$ be a field extension, $X$ a connected quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over $k$ with a rational point $x$, $p:X_K\to X$ the natural projection, $\mathcal{C}_X$ and $\mathcal{C}_{X_K}$ the Tannakian categories whose objects consist of vector bundles on $X$ and $X_K$ respectively. We give criteria for the natural homomorphism $\pi(\mathcal C_{X_K},x_K)\to\pi(\mathcal C_X,x)_K$ to be an isomorphism. Suppose further $X$ is geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$. As applications, we prove base change isomorphisms for $\pi^{\acute{e}t},\pi^{E\acute{e}t}$ under arbitrary extensions and for $\pi^S,\pi^N,\pi^{EN}$ under arbitrary algebraic extensions; a cuspidal cubic curve example shows that it can fail for purely transcendental extensions. In positive characteristic, base change isomorphism holds for $\pi^{Loc}$ and $\pi^{ELoc}$ under separable algebraic extensions; an elliptic curve example shows that it can fail for finite purely inseparable extensions.
item.dc:creator: Lingguang Li, Niantao Tian

item.title: On Fujita's conjecture for a general hyperk\"ahler manifold in the standard series of examples
item.description: arXiv:2602.12439v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the moduli spaces $\mathcal{V}(K3)_{d,t}^n$ and $\mathcal{V}(\text{Kum})_{d,t}^n$ of polarized hyperk\"ahler manifolds of $\text{Hilb}^n(K3)$-type and $\text{Kum}^n$-type respectively, with polarization with square $2d$ and divisibility $t$, we study general base point freeness and very ampleness of the polarization. We provide conditions, in terms of $n, d, t$ that guarantee that the general polarization, in any connected component of these moduli spaces, to be base point free or very ample.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pilastro

item.title: A Known M-Curve of Degree 8 in OSCAR
item.description: arXiv:2603.12985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show how the computer algebra system OSCAR can be used to retrace geometric constructions of plane algebraic curves and provide topologically correct and visually pleasing drawings. The approach is illustrated on Shustin's construction from 1987 of a particular M-curve of degree eight. We arrive at an explicit homogeneous trivariate polynomial with rational coefficients, and we provide a computational proof of all claimed properties of Shustin's original article.
item.dc:creator: Anne Fr\"uhbis-Kr\"uger, Michael Joswig, Lars Kastner

item.title: Transmission permutations and Demazure products in Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
item.description: arXiv:2604.03895v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A line bundle on a curve with two marked points can be special in many ways, as measured by the global sections of all of its twists by these points. All of this information is conveniently packaged into a permutation, which we call the transmission permutation. We prove that when twice-marked curves are chained together, these permutations are composed via the Demazure product; in reverse, bundles with given permutation can be enumerated via reduced decompositions of a permutation. This paper demonstrates the utility of transmission permutations by giving a short derivation of the basic dimension bounds of both classical Brill--Noether theory and Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory in a unified framework. The difference between the two cases derives from taking permutations in either symmetric groups or affine symmetric groups.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Pflueger

item.title: Generalized Howe curves of genus 4, 5, and 6 with completely decomposable Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2604.18074v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superspecial curves are important objects in number theory and algebraic geometry, and the existence of such a curve of genus $g \geq 4$ is an open problem, for general characteristics $p > 0$. As a computational approach to this problem, Kudo-Harashita-Howe (2020) showed that a superspecial curve of genus 4 exists in each characteristic $p$ with $7 < p < 20000$. Their method restricted attention to a specific class of curves, known as Howe curves, for which superspeciality is reduced to those of curves of genus at most 2. In this paper, we focus on a more specific class of curves, namely Howe curves whose Jacobians decompose into a product of four elliptic curves. By restricting our attention to such curves, the superspeciality reduces to the supersingularity of elliptic curves, which enables us to construct a superspecial curve of genus 4 more efficiently than Kudo-Harashita-Howe's method. As our first main result, we confirmed by computer the existence of such superspecial curves of genus 4 in characteristics $p$ with $20000 < p < 10^6$. Using a similar approach, we also propose constructions of superspecial curves of genera 5 and 6 from only supersingular elliptic curves. Furthermore, computational experiments establish the existence of superspecial curves of genus 5 (resp. genus 6) in characteristics $p$ with $13 < p < 10^5$ (resp. $7 < p < 10^5$).
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ohashi

item.title: Conifold Gap for the Quintic Threefold
item.description: arXiv:2609.13921v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the all-genus conifold gap conjecture for the Gromov--Witten (GW) theories of the quintic threefold, other smooth Fermat Calabi--Yau threefold hypersurfaces, and local $\mathbb P^2$, as well as for the FJRW theories associated with these hypersurfaces. Our proof uses Mixed Spin P-field (MSP) theory and analogous master-space constructions. The central object is the \emph{cone-vertex theory}. We express this theory as a translation of the point CohFT via a formal Laplace transform and prove a universal conifold gap theorem for the resulting translated theories. The master-space construction then transfers the gap from the cone-vertex theory to the GW and FJRW theories.
item.dc:creator: Huai-Liang Chang, Shuai Guo, Lei You, Huaigong Zhang

item.title: Hodge and Hodge-Witt polygons under specialization
item.description: arXiv:2610.05892v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that, in equal characteristic $p$, the Hodge-Witt polygon can only move down and domino numbers can only increase under specialization in smooth proper families. We also show that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal{O}_C$ lies on or above the Hodge-Witt polygon of its special fiber, where $C$ is a complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We further show that, in this mixed-characteristic setting, if the crystalline cohomology of the special fiber is torsion-free in degrees $n$ and $n+1$, then the degree-$n$ Hodge polygon of the generic fiber lies on or below the abstract Hodge polygon of the special fiber. We illustrate these comparisons with explicit examples.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang

item.title: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13528v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.
item.dc:creator: Dasheng Wei

item.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.25177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\C$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Guorui Ma

item.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.31379v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from \(2\), and let \(V\) have dimension four over \(K\). The Drinfeld upper half-spaces of \(V\) and \(\Lambda^2V\) define compatible open analytic subsets of \(\Pp(V)\), \(\Gr(2,V)\), and \(\Flag(1,2;V)\). Both restricted incidence projections are smooth and surjective. For every torsion-free discrete subgroup of \(\PGL(V)(K)\), the three actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the incidence correspondence descends to smooth analytic quotients. These domains contain an explicit flag defined over an unramified extension of degree seven. A symplectic form on \(V\) equips the projective domain with a contact structure and places the Grassmannian domain in \(\Sp_4/(\Sp_2\times\Sp_2)\). For torsion-free discrete symplectic groups, this contact structure descends to the quotient. Free discrete symplectic groups of every finite rank at least two give contact threefolds whose underlying Berkovich spaces have the homotopy type of a bouquet of circles. Every quotient of the projective domain by a torsion-free discrete group preserving the contact distribution is noncompact. For every torsion-free discrete projective linear group, the flag quotient and all fibers of its two incidence projections are noncompact; both projections are nonproper.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Verjovsky

item.title: Leafrians, Frobenius splittings, and moduli spaces over Poisson surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31619v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Poisson surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, and let $s\in H^0(X,\omega_X^{-1})$ be nonzero. We construct an anticanonical section associated to $s$, called the leafrian, on moduli spaces $M$ of stable objects on $X$, including the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons. The leafrian splits $M$ if and only if $s^{p-1}$ Frobenius splits the base. It is invariant under the Hamiltonian flows of Bottacin's Poisson structure on $M$, so every compatibly split subvariety of $M$ is a Poisson subvariety. Furthermore, the leafrian extends to an anticanonical section on the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$, and splits $\bar M$ under the same criterion. As a consequence, in characteristic zero, for $X$ a smooth projective Poisson surface with a smooth or empty anticanonical divisor and $\rho>0$ (positive leaf rank), the Gieseker compactification $\bar M$ satisfies Kodaira-type cohomology vanishing, including singular $\bar M$.
item.dc:creator: Jun Peng

item.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and prove that every vector bundle of rank at least three admits smooth connected simply branched spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.41287v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for signatures \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]
item.dc:creator: Scott Mullane

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
item.dc:creator: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis

item.title: Large N instantons, BPS states, and the replica limit
item.description: arXiv:2403.14462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the relation between large N instantons and conventional instantons, focusing on matrix models and topological strings. We show that the resurgent properties of the perturbative series at fixed but arbitrary N, including the replica limit N = 0, can be obtained from large N instantons. In the case of topological strings, it has been conjectured that the resurgent structure encoded by large N instantons is closely related to the spectrum of BPS states. We give direct evidence for this connection in the case of Seiberg-Witten theory and other topological string models, and we show in detail how the resurgent properties at fixed N follow from the large N theory, and therefore can be used to obtain information on BPS invariants.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Marino, Maximilian Schwick

item.title: Igusa Stacks and the Cohomology of Shimura Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2408.01348v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct functorial Igusa stacks for all Hodge-type Shimura varieties, proving a conjecture of Scholze and extending earlier results of the fourth-named author for PEL-type Shimura varieties. Using the Igusa stack, we construct a sheaf on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ that controls the cohomology of the corresponding Shimura variety. We use this sheaf and the spectral action of Fargues-Scholze to prove a compatibility between the cohomology of Shimura varieties of Hodge type and the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Fargues-Scholze, generalizing the Eichler-Shimura relation of Blasius-Rogawski to arbitrary level at $p$. When the given Shimura variety is proper, we show moreover that the sheaf is perverse, which allows us to prove new torsion vanishing results for the cohomology of Shimura varieties.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Daniels, Pol van Hoften, Dongryul Kim, Mingjia Zhang

item.title: Categorification of $k$-Schur functions and refined Macdonald positivity
item.description: arXiv:2505.23202v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a substantial part of the categorification framework for $k$-Schur functions proposed in Chen's Ph.D.\ thesis, written under the supervision of Mark Haiman. More precisely, we realize $k$-Schur functions as the graded characters of a distinguished family of objects in a certain module category and establish module-theoretic analogues of several foundational properties of $k$-Schur functions. A final part of Chen's framework predicts a homological characterization of modules admitting filtrations by these distinguished objects; we establish this characterization under an additional combinatorial hypothesis. In addition, we unconditionally prove that modules arising in this framework admit filtrations whose subquotients are affine Demazure modules of level $k$. As a consequence, modified Macdonald polynomials expand positively in the characters of affine Demazure modules. This may be viewed as a homological refinement of Macdonald positivity, arising from an intrinsic $\mathrm{ext}$-orthogonality condition on the corresponding Garsia--Haiman modules. We also prove the combinatorial hypothesis for $m \le 2k$ in the appendix and verify it computationally for $m\leq 19$, yielding $k$-Schur positivity of modified Macdonald polynomials in these cases. Our approach builds on our previous work on the algebraic and geometric realization of Catalan symmetric functions, a class encompassing both $k$-Schur and Hall--Littlewood functions.
item.dc:creator: Syu Kato

item.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2509.02239v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
item.dc:creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Prashanth Raman

item.title: On F-pure thresholds and quasi-F-purity of hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.06211v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that quasi-$F$-pure but not $F$-pure isolated quasi-homogeneous hypersurface singularities necessarily have $F$-pure threshold $1 - \frac{1}{p}$. This extends work of Bhatt and Singh beyond the Calabi-Yau case. We also classify the (quasi)-$F$-purity of Fermat hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jack J Garzella, Vignesh Jagathese

item.title: Derived graded modules
item.description: arXiv:2601.19164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of the $\infty$-category of (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over a $G$-graded ring $R$ for a torsion-free abelian group $G$, and we study its foundational properties. Moreover, we prove a categorical equivalence between (complete) derived $G$-graded modules over $R$ and derived (formal) comodules over a certain comonad constructed from the group ring $R[G]$ of $G$ over $R$.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ishizuka, Shou Yoshikawa

item.title: On uniform large genus asymptotics of Witten's intersection numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.15233v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Following ideas from [14], we give a uniform large genus asymptotics for primitive psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of stable algebraic curves, and extend this result including insertions of zeros in a certain uniform way. Application to a particular formal solution of the Painlev\'e I equation is given. We also use a method from [14] to give a new proof of the polynomiality conjecture on large genus asymptotic expansions of psi-class intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Jindong Guo, Di Yang, Don Zagier

item.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
item.description: arXiv:2604.20091v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.
item.dc:creator: Bryden Cais, Douglas Ulmer

item.title: On the regularity index of the minimum distance function in projective nested Cartesian codes
item.description: arXiv:2604.20729v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a projective nested product of fields and let $\delta_X(d)$ be the minimum distance in degree $d\geq 1$ of the projective nested Cartesian code $C_X(d)$. The regularity index ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ of the minimum distance function $\delta_X$ is the minimum integer $d_0\geq 0$ such that $\delta_X(d)=1$ for $d\geq d_0$.
