We give a formula for ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ by determining an indicator function of least degree for each point of $X$ and using the fact that ${\rm reg}(\delta_X)$ is the ${\rm v}$-number of the vanishing ideal $I_X$ of $X$. Then we give an arithmetical criterion that characterizes when $X$ is Cayley--Bacharach.
item.dc:creator: Cicero Carvalho, Maria Vaz Pinto, Rafael H. Villarreal

item.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2607.06285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.
item.dc:creator: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Riccardo Zuffetti

item.title: Invariant Shape Analysis of Surfaces with Spherical Topology
item.description: arXiv:2609.39567v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every real spherical harmonic of even degree is congruent to its mirror image. We prove that a real spherical harmonic of odd degree $n\ge3$ with distinct Maxwell axes is congruent to its mirror image if and only if the hyperelliptic curve of genus $n-1$ defined by its binary form has a reduced automorphism of even order whose lift acts on the form by $-1$. We then determine the locus of these curves: it is the locus of curves with an extra involution if and only if $n-1$ is a power of two, and otherwise it also contains, for each even divisor $k$ of $n-1$ with odd cofactor $d\ge3$, an irreducible family $y^2=x K(x^{2k})$, $\deg K=d$, with generic reduced automorphism group $\Z/2k$. For $n=3$ the condition is the vanishing of the skew invariant of the binary sextic. As an application, the invariants of the truncated spherical harmonic expansion of a genus-zero surface, in a conformal parameterization normalized by its conformal barycenter, give a descriptor that is exactly invariant under parameterization, position and scale, records handedness, and is stable in the orbit distance.
item.dc:creator: Tanush Shaska

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.23778v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith--Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $\mathcal E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that this dg algebra fits into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer--Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg $\mathcal E_M$-modules and the derived category of \mbox{$D$-modules} on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra $\mathcal E_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jack Jeffries, Devlin Mallory, Claudia Miller, Josh Pollitz, Eamon Quinlan-Gallego
